title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 386-388 of the 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck has defined an enlarged profinite 'Teichmüller-Galois' group \tilde M_{0,3}. Its elements are systems (φ,ψ,f), or rather (α,β,f), that act on the profinite fundamental group(oid) of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, with the S_3-symmetry built in. He has just written down an explicit map on such systems, u ↦ \underline{u} = μ·( u  εt ; -t  εu ). On the previous page he checked by brute-force matrix computation that it is multiplicative: \underline{u}'' = \underline{u}'\underline{u}, using the relation t'^2+u'^2 = ε'/μ'. This gives a homomorphism φ': \tilde M_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)' := GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}.

This page does three things:
(i) It ends the remark that the computation should sit inside a 'tapis d'algèbre linéaire'. The formulas should make sense in a group like GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}, and then for an arbitrary ring A, with GL(2,Ẑ)' replaced by GL(2,A) itself. He leaves this for later ('Peut-être y reviendrai-je finalement').
(ii) It pulls back the central extension 1→{±1}→GL(2,Ẑ)→GL(2,Ẑ)/±1→1 along φ'. This defines a central extension \tilde N_{1,1} of \tilde M_{0,3} by {±1}, together with a morphism of extensions (19) whose middle arrow is φ: \tilde N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ).
(iii) A crossed-out start defines \tilde T^+_{1,1} as the inverse image in \tilde N_{1,1} of the 'geometric' subgroup (\tilde C^+_{0,3}, called ≃ SL(2,Z)^). This is redone correctly on the next page: the inverse image of \hat T^+_{0,3} is \hat T^+_{1,1} ≃ SL(2,Z)^. That yields diagram (20), with \hat T^+_{1,1} → SL(2,Ẑ), \tilde N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ), and the quotient Γ^~ → Ẑ^× (χ, presumably cyclotomic-type) via det.

Modern reading: this is a 'universal Tate-module representation' of a GT-type group. The ±1 extension plays the role of the elliptic involution, passing from genus-0 data (the S_3-orbifold of M_{0,4}, with π1 ≈ PSL(2,Z)^) to the genus-1 group N_{1,1}, with π1 ≈ SL(2,Z)^. The aim is to extend the classical modular representation π1(M_{1,1}/Q) → GL(2,Ẑ) (det = cyclotomic character) to the larger group \tilde M_{0,3}. Restricted to geometric parts it is the congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ).
errors: The crossed-out passage calls the subgroup \tilde C^+_{0,3} ⊂ \tilde M_{0,3} '≃ SL(2,Z)^'. But its inverse image in the ±1-extension is what should be ≃ SL(2,Z)^; the genus-0 subgroup should be the PSL-type quotient. The next page corrects this by saying the inverse image of \hat T^+_{0,3} is \hat T^+_{1,1} ≃ SL(2,Z)^, which is probably why the passage was struck.
No mathematical error in the pullback construction itself (pullback of a central extension along a homomorphism is formal).

Gap: the compatibility of φ' with the classical 'modular' homomorphism on M_{0,3} ⊂ \tilde M_{0,3} is admitted without proof on the next page. The identification of the inverse image of M_{0,3} with N_{1,1} depends on it.

ideas.what: Pull back the central extension GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 along φ' to get a ±1 central extension \tilde N_{1,1} of \tilde M_{0,3}, i.e. pass from genus (0,3)/(0,4) data to genus (1,1) via the elliptic involution.
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of central extensions; the elliptic-involution extension SL(2,Z) → PSL(2,Z) at the level of GT-type groups (genus 0 → genus 1 lifting of GT actions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lifting GT/Galois actions from genus 0 to M_{1,1}: Nakamura, Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (late 1990s–2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the passage between M_{0,4} and M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z) in general terms; this explicit construction is not published to my knowledge

ideas.what: A homomorphism φ: \tilde N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ) extending the profinite congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ), with det giving a character of the quotient (diagram 20 on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Universal Tate-module / modular representation of a GT-type group; analogue of π1(M_{1,1,Q}) → GL_2(Ẑ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for Gal(Q̄/Q) (Tate module of the universal elliptic curve). Analogues for \widehat{GT} acting on the profinite B_3/SL_2(Z) appear in work of Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and others

ideas.what: The explicit matrix formulas for φ' should hold in GL(2,A) for an arbitrary ring A (a 'linear-algebra carpet' behind the computation).
ideas.modern_name: Making the representation algebraic / defined over arbitrary coefficient rings (group-scheme-type formulas)

missed.claim: Grothendieck suspects that the explicit formulas defining \tilde M_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)/±1 come from a general linear-algebra structure valid over any ring A, with target GL(2,A). He explicitly postpones developing this.
missed.quote: puis on remplace Ẑ par un anneau quelconque, et bien sûr GL(2,Ẑ)' par GL(2,A) lui-même. Peut-être y reviendrai-je finalement....
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An 'algebraic' version of the map from a GT-type group to GL_2 would clarify how the Galois-Teichmüller / GT action on genus 0 induces the modular (Tate-module) representation in genus 1. It might relate to pro-unipotent/elliptic GT (Enriquez, Hain–Matsumoto). Likely of modest novelty.

missed.claim: Explicit construction of a ±1 central extension \tilde N_{1,1} of the genus-0 group \tilde M_{0,3}, mapping to GL(2,Ẑ) with SL(2,Z)^ as geometric part. This is an early, explicit formula-level version of lifting GT-type symmetries to M_{1,1} together with a 'cyclotomic' determinant.
missed.quote: on obtient, par image inverse de l'extension centrale GL(2,Ẑ) de GL(2,Ẑ)' par {±1}, une extension centrale de \tilde M_{0,3} par {±1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of documentary interest for the history of genus-0 → genus-1 GT liftings. The underlying mathematics is likely known to specialists in the Nakamura–Schneps line.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a formal pullback of a central extension, plus a postponed generalization to arbitrary rings. The broader idea of an explicit homomorphism from his GT-like group to GL(2,Ẑ) is interesting historically but close to known later work.
transcription_corrections: Line 'on [-déduit-] {+obtient+}': the image shows 'on déduit' with 'centrale' inserted (as 'centrale' / 'cantrale') above 'GL(2,Ẑ)' on the next line, i.e. 'de l'extension centrale GL(2,Ẑ) de GL(2,Ẑ)' par {±1}'.
'par produit \tilde N_{1,1}' is likely 'que je noterai \tilde N_{1,1}' or similar; the hand reads 'par p... \tilde N_{1,1}', not 'produit'.
'un un homo d'extensions' should read 'un homo[morphisme] d'extensions' ('et on a un homo d'extensions').

In diagram (19) the top-row arrow \tilde N_{1,1} → \tilde M_{0,3} carries a struck-out symbol (\tilde{\mathcal C}?) before \tilde M_{0,3}. The vertical arrows are φ (middle) and φ' (right), as transcribed.

The final paragraph is entirely crossed out in the image, including the bracketed alternative notations (\tilde T^+_{1,1}, \tilde{\mathcal C}^+_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Z)^, \tilde N^+_{1,1}). It reads roughly: 'Par ailleurs, désignons par \tilde T^+_{1,1} l'image inverse de \tilde{\mathcal C}^+_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Z)^ ⊂ \tilde M_{0,3} dans l'extension \tilde N^+_{1,1} de \tilde M_{0,3} par ±1, on a une [flèche] \tilde T^+_{1,1} → N_{1,1}'.
